key_insight: A fully local multi-agent AI system can deidentify multimodal hospital data with near-complete accuracy while preserving clinically important content.
clinical_relevance: This could make it safer to reuse sensitive hospital data for AI development, research, and cross-modal clinical workflows without losing key medical context.
method: Built a modular local framework combining multimodal LLMs, task-specific neural networks, and rule-based transformations.
Benchmarked 16 orchestrator configurations on public and institutional data spanning text, head CT, face images, handwriting, and audio.
Compared performance against leading proprietary and open-source deidentification solutions.
evidence_signal: In a benchmark including 250 MIMIC-IV patients with synthetic PII plus local multimodal data, the best local configuration reached 98.80% per-patient sensitivity and 99.82% per-PII sensitivity, with 99.60% critical clinical preservation.
watch_item: Results are strong in benchmark testing, but real-world deployment still needs careful validation for rare edge cases, modality drift, and workflow integration.
paper_title: The Multimodal Anonymizer: a fully local multi-agent AI system for medical data deidentification
